Import a scan#

Bring the capture you already have — from a phone or tablet with LiDAR, a photogrammetry or capture app, a 3D tour platform's export bundle, or a laser scanner — and get a cleaned, streamed Verse scene: the right way up, in metres, with the capture's faults fixed, on a laptop and on a phone.

This page covers importing: formats, orientation, units, what the cleanup fixes and its limits.

In the app#

On the upload screen, choose Import a scan:

  1. Where is it from? Phone or tablet LiDAR · Photogrammetry or capture app · 3D tour export bundle · Laser scanner or point cloud. Each source shows what to export and narrows the file picker to the formats it makes.
  2. 3D tour export bundle only: choose Textured mesh (the walkable space) or Point cloud (the bundle's cloud). If you have a link to a hosted tour instead of the bundle, paste it under Have a tour link instead? — the app tells you what to do (see Tour links).
  3. More options (rarely needed): Up axis and Units override the automatic choice; Clean up the scan (on by default) can be unticked to publish the capture as captured.
  4. Choose the scan file, or drop it on the page while the panel is open. The usual checks run, then the upload starts.

Formats#

SourceFormatsWhat happens
Phone or tablet LiDAR.usdz, .glb, .ply (mesh or points), .obj in a .zip with its .mtl and textures, .e57Meshes are converted to GLB where needed and cleaned; point clouds are packed and streamed
Photogrammetry or capture app.glb / .gltf (embedded), zipped .obj, .ply mesh, .usdz, Gaussian-splat .ply (3DGS) or .splatThe same; a splat capture is packed as a splat
3D tour export bundlethe bundle's .zip as downloaded (an OBJ mesh with its textures, cloud.xyz, colour floor plans)Textured mesh: its OBJ is converted (the bundle is Z-up, metres) and cleaned. Point cloud: its cloud.xyz is unpacked and packed as a cloud
Laser scanner or point cloud.e57, .las / .laz, .ply points, .xyz / .pts text, or a zip carrying onePacked into a streamed point cloud (every scan in an E57 is merged)

Every import above is exercised by web/test/fix-verify-scan-import.mjs, except LAS / LAZ: they ride the existing point-cloud reader (fix-verify-cloud.mjs packs a LAS file and recognises a LAZ header).

Up axis and units#

A capture often does not say which way is up, or what unit it is in. glTF is Y-up in metres by definition and USD declares both (upAxis, metersPerUnit), so those frames are kept. For the others the server decides before anything else is measured (the cleanup's thresholds are in metres):

Up. The evidence is which way the surfaces face. A capture sees the tops of things — the floor, table tops, seats — and rarely their undersides, so the area-weighted sum of the surface normals points up; opposite walls cancel. The strongest axis wins only when it is clearly ahead (at least 3 % of the total surface, and twice the runner-up). Otherwise the format's convention stands: Z-up for E57 and LAS, Y-up for OBJ, PLY and text clouds (phone capture apps write Y-up). A tour bundle is always read Z-up. A point cloud without normals has no surface evidence, so it follows the convention. Every rotation is a quarter or half turn about an axis — the floor's residual tilt is then levelled by the cleanup.

Units. A capture is human-scale. After orientation, a file at most 40 units tall and 500 across is read as metres. Otherwise centimetres, then millimetres, are tried: the first that makes the height between 1.8 m and 15 m wins. Inches and feet are never guessed.

Overriding. In the app: More options → Up axis / Units. Through the API: X-Verse-Up: auto | x | y | z | -x | -y | -z and X-Verse-Units: m | cm | mm | in | ft. An unreadable value is ignored. A USD or FBX file's declared frame is applied by its converter and is not overridden.

What the gate measures: one procedural 4 × 3 m room, 2.5 m tall, written as a Z-up centimetre OBJ zip, a millimetre PLY mesh, a Z-up USDZ declaring centimetres, a tour bundle, a Z-up PLY point cloud with normals, a millimetre XYZ cloud and a Z-up E57 — every one lands as a 4.00 × 2.50 × 3.00 m room, Y-up, with the floor at y = 0 (meshes: the published GLB's bounds; clouds: the packed cloud's root points).

Cleanup#

Meshes go through the existing scan cleanup: floor levelled and put at y = 0, floating debris removed, small holes filled, light baked into the texture evened out. An import from the panel always asks for it (X-Verse-Scan: clean); untick Clean up the scan (X-Verse-Scan: off) to publish exactly as exported. With off, an explicit up axis or unit still applies — the orientation step runs alone, nothing else changes.

On the gate's synthetic room the cleanup removes the three floating crumbs and fills the 16 × 16 cm hole in the far wall, on every mesh import.

Tour links#

A link to a hosted tour cannot be imported: fetching a tour's geometry needs the tour platform's API access, which a Verse server does not have. Paste a link into the app and it recognises it (with the model's id) and answers: ask the model's owner — or anyone they gave export rights — to download the model's export bundle from their tour account, then upload that zip unchanged. Nothing is fetched. Other links get a plain "download the file first" answer.

Limits#

The same rules as every upload, published by GET /v1/limits under scanImport:

LimitValueWhere it is enforced
File size512 MBthe upload (one-shot and resumable begin)
Conversion (OBJ, PLY mesh, USDZ)15 min (VERSE_CONVERT_TIMEOUT_S)the converter
Cleanup10 min (VERSE_SCAN_CLEAN_TIMEOUT_S)scan-clean
Packing a cloud or a splat30 min per attemptcloud-pack / splat-pack
Whole job45 min wall clockthe job
Point cloud200 million pointsthe preflight and cloud-pack
Splat capture4 million splatsthe preflight and splat-pack
Import from a linknot available (linkImport: false)—

A cleanup that cannot run never fails the upload: the capture is published as captured and the record says why.

Errors#

A broken file fails with one of the usual friendly errors (a sentence and its fix, plus errorInfo.code); the raw detail stays in the server log. The gate checks:

FileError
A GLB cut off part-waycorrupt_file
A PLY whose header promises more points than it holdscloud_invalid
A PLY announcing 300 million pointscloud_too_many
An E57 with a valid header and garbage after itcloud_invalid
A zip with no scan in itunsupported_format
A USDZ whose layer is not USDbim_invalid ("the file could not be parsed (line 3, column 8)")
Text that is not a point cloudcloud_invalid
A file that is not a model at allunsupported_format
A scan over 512 MBfile_too_large, at begin

API#

POST /v1/ingest (or the resumable begin / part / commit) with:

HeaderBegin bodyMeaning
X-Verse-Scan: clean | offscanclean (the panel's default) or publish as captured
X-Verse-Upupwhich file axis is up; auto infers
X-Verse-Unitsunitsthe file's unit (an OBJ without it keeps the converter's own guess unless it is a scan import)
X-Verse-Kind: cloudkinda point cloud, or a tour bundle's cloud

The finished record carries what was done: for a mesh, scan.frame (up, upMode, unit, unitMode, size); for a cloud, frame; and a plain-words line in fixes, e.g. "Normalised the scan: turned it upright (its z axis was up — its surfaces showed which way is up) and read its units as centimetres (250 units tall reads as 2.50 m in cm) — now 4.00 × 2.50 × 3.00 m." upMode / unitMode is inferred, convention, asked or kept.

The tools take the same choices: scan-clean in.glb -o out.glb --up auto --units auto [--up-convention z] and cloud-pack in.e57 -o out.vpc --up auto --units auto (the decision is printed as cloud-frame: {json}). The shared rules live in crates/verse-compile/src/scan_frame.rs (unit-tested); the app and the server share web/playground/scan-import.js.

The gate#

web/test/fix-verify-scan-import.mjs (ports 9850–9859) generates every input itself (make-scan-import-fixtures.mjs; the E57 is written by the e57 crate's writer, examples/make-scan-e57; the splat comes from the repository's sample splat) — no customer files, nothing downloaded. It checks the shared module, detection of every fixture, every importer end to end, the normalised geometry, the bad files and limits, a render of every import on renderer tier A (WebGPU, desktop) and tier C (WebGL2, phone viewport), the card (sources, help, tour link, a picked file's upload and its result, a 375 px phone), and these docs. Output: web/test/out/scan-import/ (screenshots, metrics.json).

On Linux without a GPU, tier A runs on SwiftShader through Vulkan (--enable-features=Vulkan --use-vulkan=swiftshader --use-angle=swiftshader): the default headless WebGPU path loses its device every few seconds there.

Known gaps#

  • Hosted tour links are recognised, not imported — that needs the tour platform's API access. Use the export bundle.
  • The fixtures are synthetic. They have the shapes the apps export (formats, frames, units, a tour bundle's layout), not real captures; the cleanup on real phone captures is measured by fix-verify-scans.mjs, which needs four CC-BY captures (docs/attributions.md).
  • Inches and feet are never inferred; ask with X-Verse-Units.
  • Small objects in centimetres or millimetres (under 40 units tall) read as metres, and taller ones are sized as a room would be; ask with X-Verse-Units.
  • Up for a cloud without normals follows the convention (Z for E57 and LAS, Y otherwise); a Y-up E57 without normals needs X-Verse-Up: y.
  • Splat captures are packed as exported: the up/units step does not run on splats. Tier C has no splat renderer (it says so); compressed .spz splats are not read.
  • Untextured room-layout USDZ files (walls and furniture as plain boxes) are not covered by the gate.
  • Converter version: the gate's OBJ / PLY conversions ran here on Blender 4.0.2; production pins Blender 5.0.1.
